content.thinking:
I'm planning the fox design: a standing kitsune with a fanned arrangement of nine tails and glowing blue spirit-flame accents around the body and tail tips, then thinking through which builder API to use for constructing it.

Checking which samples export their build function with createBuilder and returning b.root, and making sure I import only the modules I'll actually use from paint, texture, and toon kits to avoid unused-import errors. I'm sketching the body as a swept shape along the spine with tapering elliptical cross-sections from hips to chest, using cel-shaded fur coloring for the coat.

For the kitsune design, I'm settling on an ivory-white coat with crimson kumadori markings, using furEdge to blend two tones along a belly line, and paint functions to add dark crimson socks on the legs. The head will use a scaled sphere skull with a sculpted muzzle and extruded triangular ears.

Working out placement: eye decals on the skull at specific azimuth/elevation angles, a dark nose sphere at the muzzle tip, a neck capsule connecting chest to head, and considering simple tuft textures for the fur ruff and tails rather than complex card systems.

Figuring out ear geometry, computing cross products to determine which direction each ear's front face points depending on left/right side, then offsetting the inner ear slightly forward along that normal.

For cheek fur I'll add white spike cones sweeping outward, and then build nine tails fanning from a base point behind the body, each as a curved path with a tapering radius profile.

Computing tail fan angles and curve points...

Checking max tail height against fox body proportions, then figuring out tail tip coloring using a gradient paint applied along the computed curve path rather than discrete color bands.

Now I'm designing the glowing flame effect for each tail tip, using crossed extruded teardrop outlines so the flame reads from multiple viewing angles, with a soft glow color applied to each.

I'm figuring out how to scatter tufted fur-texture cards onto the tail surfaces using a sweep-based surface function, uncertain whether it accepts arrays of sweeps, so I'll fall back to applying it per-tail with a modest number of randomized cards to keep things safe.

Now I'm adding floating foxfire orbs (hitodama) with flame tails scattered around the ground at varying heights and radii, making sure the lowest orb stays above the fox's paw height, plus planning decal-based face markings like red kumadori streaks and a gold diamond mark on the skull.

I'm placing the forehead decal using elevation/azimuth hit coordinates to position a crimson tri-diamond mark, then adding mirrored cheek streaks, before moving to a golden collar swept as a closed path around the tilted neck axis.

For the collar I'm switching to a torus geometry aligned with the neck direction vector, calculating the right position and radius so it sits naturally without being buried, then adding a hanging bell pendant at the chest front.

I'm also considering gold anklets as torus shapes on the front legs, gold rings on the ear edges, and a flowing red sash sweeping back from the collar knot using a catmull curve with a box cross-section.

Still working out leg geometry... building segmented front legs with swept curves from shoulder to paw, tapering radii, and a flattened sphere for the paw shape touching the ground.

Still shaping the paw and body geometry...

For the ruff and fur clusters I'm planning spiky cones pointing down-forward at the chest, plus tuft cards scattered across the neck, tails, and cheeks using a flame-like ivory leaf shape with a subtle warm stroke. I'm setting up the card scatter function to place these tufts onto surface hit frames with size, lean, and bend variation driven by a seeded random generator.

Now I'm working out eye placement on the skull sphere, sizing the eye decals and positioning them at roughly 35-40° azimuth to sit naturally on a fox-like muzzle, and settling on a warm gold-amber iris color like "#f5b020". I'm also sketching the muzzle sweep from the skull center forward, figuring out its radius and tip position relative to the skull's front edge.

Still placing facial features...

Skipping the ear ring idea, I'm deciding against extra bells and paw flames, keeping just the orbs and forehead flame for simplicity. I'll focus on the tail tip flame, placing it at the end of the tail path with a slight downward offset and defining a flame function with height and color parameters for the glowing effect.

Still writing flame geometry...

I'm setting glow colors for the tail flames and giving the forehead decal mark a fiery glow effect, then adding a hub sphere where the tails emerge from the rump.

Now I'm computing the tail path geometry, fanning nine tails outward with varying angles and tapering radii so the central tail sits tallest while side tails curve sideways with less height.

Still working out the tail curvature...

For the coloring, I'm thinking ivory base fading into crimson tips, kitsune-style, maybe with a hint of gold rings around each tail for extra ornamentation.

Adding gold rings and ribbons...

Now I'm placing a bell pendant hanging at the front-bottom of the collar torus, computing the position via the perpendicular-to-axis direction, with a small gold sphere and three crimson tassel spikes dangling downward from a nearby base point.

Next I want to add body markings -- a crimson kumadori-style stripe running along the spine, defined as a paint function that checks proximity to the x=0 centerline with a zigzag pattern varying along z, falling back to the regular coat paint elsewhere, nested inside the cel shading wrapper.

Still writing paint logic... then I'll apply the leg sock paint to legs and the body paint to haunches, add a few thin whisker capsules sweeping out from the muzzle sides, and skip eyebrow details for now.

Beyond that I'm skipping teeth and any ground plane since the fox just stands in place, and planning out spirit orb positions with flame-colored material. For the neck and chest ruff I'll scatter card details across the neck surface with a minimum distance filter, and scatter fewer cards along the tail, relying on a seeded random generator for consistent placement.

I'm also sketching out small ink-colored claw spikes at the front paws and deciding against adding toe-bean spheres, then exporting the build function along with metadata like name, description, and style.

Now I'm drafting a flame helper that builds layered glow shapes with an outer and core color, using extrusion with defined thickness and smoothing, and thinking through how the outline points should wind so the shape closes properly.

I'm working out the extrusion thickness axis using a cross product so the flame shapes are oriented correctly along each direction, then confirming the glow wrapper just returns the part so meshes stay accessible for the card components. For the forehead mark, I'm designing a small decal texture—a crimson diamond with a dot—and figuring out how to position it on the head sphere by finding a hit point and aligning it with the surface normal at that elevation.

Now I'm sketching the cheek streak decal as a tapered polygon shape in SVG, working out placement angles (mirrored by side, positioned below the eye) and leaving the roll rotation unresolved for now. I'm also setting the eye hit positions based on azimuth and elevation to match the skull's scale, then starting to tally up the total part count including the tails.

Checking unused imports and making sure helper functions like catmull, glow, and INK are actually used where needed, while confirming the tail path points and ribbon radius function are typed correctly.

I'm placing orb positions around the body with glow effects and flames above each, then finalizing the code.
